narrative:
The model determined that you have a 33% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

Three pieces of information weighed most heavily in this decision. First, the fact that you have a guarantor for the loan worked strongly in your favor. Having someone willing to guarantee repayment is relatively uncommon and pushed the prediction noticeably toward approval. 

Unfortunately, two other factors pulled the decision in the opposite direction and ultimately outweighed that positive signal. Your checking account is currently in negative balance. Among approved applicants, only about 13% have a negative balance, so this situation is uncommon and signaled higher risk to the model. In addition, the loan amount you requested was substantially smaller than what most approved borrowers ask for. While a smaller loan might seem safer, in this case the model interpreted it, together with your checking-account status, as an indicator of financial pressure.

Taken together, the negative signals from your checking-account status and the requested amount were strong enough to overcome the positive effect of having a guarantor, leading to the denial.

You should focus on improving your checking-account balance and, if possible, reapply in a few months with a clearer picture of your finances. This would likely remove the strongest negative factor and improve your chances of approval. (218 words)
